# Causal Threshold Backaction

> A causal ordered threshold detector that preserves charge sectors has a
> pure-input entropy cost fixed, up to universal additive constants, by the
> input's coarse-charge entropy. A finite distributed window instrument
> supplies a matching upper bound; general-instrument bounds establish robustness.

Repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Causal-Threshold-Backaction
Working title: The Backaction Cost of Causal Threshold Measurements
Author and contact: Ruge Lin, gogoko699@gmail.com

- [Proof map](research/PROOF_MAP.md): dependencies and locations of the complete arguments.

- [Attribution](literature/ATTRIBUTION.md): primary sources and precise scope comparisons.

## Questions this repository answers

- Can a binary threshold with a certain answer create many bits of system entropy?
- How do calibration, nondisturbance inside charge sectors, and one-way causality constrain measurement backaction?
- Why does H(floor(Q/g)) determine the optimal exact pure-input cost up to constants?
- Which finite distributed instrument realizes the triangular coherence kernel?
- What changes when calibration or preservation is imperfect, and which bounds require averaging prepared phases?
- How does this differ from parity measurements, gentle noisy counting, and previously known nonlocal meter architectures?

Useful search phrases: causal threshold measurement; coarse-charge entropy;
nonsignalling measurement backaction; sector-preserving quantum instrument;
translated window meter; GHZ-like distributed measurement; Fejér kernel entropy;
semicausal Stinespring dilation; quantum serial encoding; phase-average entropy.

## Interpretation constraints

All entropy is in bits. Exact preservation covers every state in every global
charge sector. The result concerns initially pure inputs and the nonselective
retained system. The global answer is available after classical collection.
The cost is optimized over detectors for a fixed input, not a minimax quantity.
The uniform errors are additive constants; they are not a sharp large-gap rate.
General robust statements concern the specified phase average. Approximate
causality is measured in full diamond norm. Numerical checks evaluate the
explicit apparatus and identities, not the universal optimization problem.

Read AGENTS.md before editing. Citation metadata is in CITATION.cff and
references.bib. This guide helps discovery; it does not guarantee indexing.
